content.title: About
content.content: Sunflower seeds are the edible seeds of the sunflower plant (Helianthus annuus). They have a mild nutty flavor, a crunchy texture, and are typically sold without added salt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sunflower is one of the most widely cultivated crops worldwide, and its seeds are a major source of vegetable oil.
The seeds are rich in vitamin E, a powerful antioxidant.
Seeds can be used both as food and in cosmetics (oil for skin and hair).
There are several seed varieties: large ones for snacking and smaller ones for oil production.
Sunflowers attract bees and other pollinators, supporting biodiversity.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E protects cells from oxidative stress and supports skin health.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Most of the fat is polyunsaturated, including omega‑6 fatty acids important for heart health.

items.title: Source of magnesium
items.content: Magnesium aids muscle and nerve function and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: Protein supports muscle maintenance, while fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains selenium
items.content: Selenium contributes to immune function and protects against free radicals.

items.title: Seed allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sunflower seeds.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Seeds are calorie-dense, so they should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; soaking can lower its level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sunflower seeds can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, oatmeal, baked goods, or used to make homemade oil. Eating them unsalted helps control sodium intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store seeds in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
